metadata.title: Painter, Maini & Othmer (1999) PNAS 96(10):5549-5554 Pomacanthus growing-domain Turing + chemotaxis model: Fig. 3/4/8 parameter sets and the Kondo & Asai (1995) 3 -> 6 -> 12 stripe-doubling table
metadata.correction_note: The seed DOI 10.1073/pnas.96.10.5549 resolves to 'Stripe formation in juvenile Pomacanthus explained by a generalized Turing mechanism with chemotaxis' (PMID 10318921, PMCID PMC21897). Passes 1-2 and the SHA-256-pinned scout_manifest.json cite it under the non-existent title 'Stripe and spotilihood in chemotactic pattern formation'; that title is superseded by this file.

sources.citation: Painter KJ, Maini PK, Othmer HG (1999). Stripe formation in juvenile Pomacanthus explained by a generalized Turing mechanism with chemotaxis. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA 96(10):5549-5554.
Kondo S, Asai R (1995). A reaction-diffusion wave on the skin of the marine angelfish Pomacanthus. Nature 376:765-768.
Crampin EJ, Gaffney EA, Maini PK (1999). Reaction and diffusion on growing domains: scenarios for robust pattern formation. Bulletin of Mathematical Biology 61(6):1093-1120.

governing_equations.morphogens: du/dt = D_u Lap(u) + f(u,v) - (r_1 + r_2) u ;  dv/dt = D_v Lap(v) + g(u,v) - (r_1 + r_2) v   (fixed-domain form with growth dilution)
governing_equations.iridophores: dn/dt = D_n Lap(n) - div( n chi(u) grad(u) ) ;  chi(u) = chi_0 / (k + u)^2 ;  chi_0 < 0 (u is a repellent)
governing_equations.cell_dilution: none: PNAS 1999 assumes all cell types proliferate at the tissue growth rate so the total cell density stays constant
governing_equations.growth_law: L_i(t) = L_i(0) exp(r_i t), uniform dilation about the centre
governing_equations.boundary_conditions: zero flux for cells and morphogens

kinetics_fig3.source: Kondo & Asai (1995) piecewise-linear kinetics; PNAS 1999 Fig. 3 caption (the PMC caption text reads 'g(u,v) = 0.1u - 0.15 - 0.06', the dropped factor is v)

fig3_parameters_1d.initial_conditions: +/- 0.5 % random perturbation of the morphogen steady state; uniform cells n(x,0) = 1
fig3_parameters_1d.stated_result: parameters selected to give rise to the three-peak pattern corresponding to the three juvenile stripes (Fig. 1a); peak doubling of u is rapid, cell-density stripes insert gradually

fig4_parameters_2d.note: Reproduced here on a surface of revolution with isotropic growth r = 1e-4 (Fig. 3 rate) and circumference C_0 = 1.9 (same lowest transverse wavenumber as the 0.95 zero-flux DV extent); the 20 % RC/DV growth anisotropy of Fig. 4 is not reproduced (open remediation item).

fig5_breakup.stated_result: stripes become wavy and eventually convoluted on the larger domain (cf. Chaetodontoplus duboulayi); larger growth rates can suppress patterning entirely

fig8_lengyel_epstein_adult_transition.stated_result: stripe doubling during growth followed by breakup into spots as the domain approaches its final size (juvenile -> adult P. semicirculatus)
fig8_lengyel_epstein_adult_transition.note: not reproduced in this script (open remediation item)

kondo_asai_1995_pomacanthus_semicirculat.section: Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376:765-768; reproduced as PNAS 1999 Fig. 1 (a) 2 months, (b) 6 months, (c) 12 months
kondo_asai_1995_pomacanthus_semicirculat.observation: juvenile P. semicirculatus carry three vertical white stripes; as the body grows new stripes insert between the existing ones so that the inter-stripe spacing is maintained, 3 -> 6 -> 12
kondo_asai_1995_pomacanthus_semicirculat.doubling_law: N(s) = 3 s for body-length scale s in {1, 2, 4}; stripe number doubles when body length doubles because the spacing is conserved
kondo_asai_1995_pomacanthus_semicirculat.note: relative_body_length is the model-side scale factor s implied by spacing conservation, not a measured length; Kondo & Asai report sizes only qualitatively in the sources consulted

curved_surface_extension_pass3.surface: surface of revolution rho(x) about the rostro-caudal axis; metric ds^2 = (1 + rho'^2) dx^2 + rho^2 dtheta^2; Laplace-Beltrami Lap_g f = (1/(rho w)) d_x(rho/w d_x f) + (1/rho^2) d_theta^2 f, w = sqrt(1 + rho'^2)

profiles.cylinder: rho = C_0 / 2pi (Gaussian curvature K = 0; flat-rectangle control with periodic DV)
profiles.spindle: rho(X) = rho_max [0.3 + 0.7 sin(pi X)] (K = -rho'' / (rho (1 + rho'^2)^2) > 0 at mid-body)

curved_surface_extension_pass3.uniform_growth: g(t) = s(t)^2 g_0, s = exp(r t): Lap_g = Lap_g0 / s^2, morphogen dilution 2 r (Crampin, Gaffney & Maini 1999), cells undiluted (PNAS 1999 assumption)
